problem_type: clip audio preview and export contract gap
symptom: Timeline clips could not persist or render clip-local gain, mute, fade-in, or fade-out, so Agent-authored and future UI-authored audio edits had no executable preview/export path.
direct_cause: The persisted TimelineClip, renderer manifest, preview media elements, and FFmpeg audio graph had no shared clip-audio contract or envelope semantics.
class_root: Audio processing was represented only by a global preview volume and an unparameterized FFmpeg mixdown, leaving no canonical clip-local invariant across persistence, validation, preview, and export boundaries.
affected_population: Projects that need clip-local attenuation or mute on audio clips
Video clips whose embedded source audio needs attenuation, mute, or boundary fades
Agent and future UI workflows that require preview/export parity for clip audio edits
entry_points: normalizeTimeline when loading persisted or foreign timeline state
validateTimeline before timeline operations and Agent plan adoption
TimelinePreview video and BGM media-element playback
buildRenderManifestRequest and assertValidManifest at the renderer-to-Electron boundary
compileFfmpegFiltergraph for standalone audio and embedded video source audio
internal_only_reason: This change connects Nomi's existing timeline and FFmpeg boundaries using standard FFmpeg volume and afade filters; no third-party API behavior or dependency choice is being changed.
invariants: Missing clip audio settings preserve legacy unity gain, audible playback, and zero fades without changing existing default filtergraphs.
The same decibel conversion and linear frame envelope govern preview and export; positive gain remains unsupported until preview can exceed unity gain honestly.
Invalid renderer manifests fail explicitly instead of dropping malformed audio fields or silently falling back.
Image clips cannot carry clip audio processing and combined fades cannot exceed the visible clip duration.
migration: Timeline schema version remains 1. Old clips omit audio and retain exact legacy behavior. Persisted non-image audio objects are normalized to bounded values on load; renderer manifests require a complete valid audio object when the optional field is present.
residual_risks: Adjacent clip crossfade is intentionally deferred because the fixed audio track rejects overlap and the timeline has no audio-transition entity; two boundary fades would not be a real acrossfade.
Positive gain is intentionally deferred until preview uses Web Audio or another gain stage capable of matching FFmpeg above unity.
